subject: categorical detection covariate in occupancy model with false positives

messages.author: 715ca9de5bff9dae
messages.subject: categorical detection covariate in occupancy model with false positives
parts:
Hi all,


I'm trying to fit an occupancy model in jags allowing for false positive detections (pF) as well as true detection probabilities (pT).

However, rather than fitting the model with a single false positive detection probability- e.g. along the lines of 

Py[i,j,t] <- (z[i,t]*pT)+ ((1- z[i,t])*pF)

y[i,j,t] ~ dbern (Py[i,j,t])


with data y[i,j,t] representing detection/nondetection at i sites, j observations per year and t years

I instead want to fit different false positive probabilities depending on (4) population size classes recorded- so I can see whether larger recorded population counts are less likely to represent a false positive occupancy observation.
To do so I've expanded the single pF in the example above with a term giving the sum of the products of pF for each population class and a binary array specifying whether the observation contains a count in that population class (e.g. ((pF1*popclass1[i,j,t])+(pF2*popclass2[I,j,t])+…)

However, it’s clear to me from running my model on simulated data that it is not performing at all as it should, and I’m at a bit of a loss as to why. In fact, it seems that regardless of the detection parameters that I use to simulate the data, I seem to consistently get true detection (pT) and false detection (pF) for the lowest 2 population classes estimated at >0.99, and pF for the higher two population classes estimated at ~0.5.

 


 If anyone has any any ideas as to why this isn't working, or where I've gone wrong, I'd be very happy to hear them! I've attached the jags model file "pFcategorical.jags" and code used to simulate the data and run the model "code for categoricalpF.R"

 

 

All the best

Sam


Edit: I've just noticed that the problem is likely something to do with effective sample sizes- looking at the model outputs it seems as though pT.mean, pF.1 and pF.2 only have n.eff=1. Any ideas as to why this is the case?
